records.text: Civil Appeal No. 73 of 1950 arises from a judgment of the High Court of Judicature at Patna dated 26th January, 1944, which itself stemmed from a decree of the Additional Subordinate Judge of Hazaribagh in Title Suit No. 45 of 1939.
records.owner_label: CIVIL APPELLATE, JURISDICTION: Civil Appeal No. 73 of 1950
records.event: Case jurisdiction and procedural history defined

records.text: The central legal question is whether, prior to the 1929 enactment of Section 65-A of the Transfer of Property Act, a mortgagor in possession had the power to grant a permanent lease of the mortgaged property so as to bind the mortgagee.
records.event: Legal question for consideration identified

records.text: Raja Nilkanth Narain Singh mortgaged Gadi Sirampur to the Chota Nagpur Banking Association Limited on 1st August, 1914. The Bank obtained a mortgage decree on 29th November, 1921, and purchased a third share on 28th October, 1922.
records.event: Mortgage and subsequent decree details

records.text: During the pendency of mortgage proceedings, on 5th November, 1925, Wazir Narain Singh granted a permanent lease of four villages to Hiraman Ram, Manager and Karta of his joint Hindu family, and his son Chohan Ram.
records.event: Permanent lease granted during mortgage suit pendency
records.procedure: Court of Additional Subordinate Judge of Hazaribagh

records.text: An agreement was made that if Wazir Narain Singh paid Rs. 1,10,631-4-0 by 16th August, 1926, the sale would be set aside. He executed a mortgage on 14th August, 1926, to the Court of Wards to satisfy dues and set aside the sale.
records.event: Sale set aside and new mortgage executed

records.text: The Plaintiff (through the Manager of the Court of Wards) filed a suit on 4th February, 1929, to enforce the mortgage, impleading Hiraman Ram and Dilo Ram as co-defendants. A final decree for sale was passed on 18th September, 1931.
records.event: Enforcement suit and auction sale

records.text: Dilo Ram died after the mortgage decree. Hiraman Ram and his son Chohan Ram continued in actual possession. The Plaintiff filed the suit on 16th November, 1939, against them for khas possession of the villages.
records.event: Suit for khas possession filed
records.procedure: Court of Additional Subordinate Judge of Hazaribagh

records.text: Defendant 2 contended that the Plaintiff was not subrogated to the Bank's position, the decree was not binding as he was not a party, the Patta was not ended by the auction sale, and a partition occurred within a year allotting properties to him.
records.event: Defendants contesting plaintiff's claim

records.text: The Trial Court held the Plaintiff was subrogated to the Bank's position, Defendant 1 was the Manager/Karta, Defendant 2 was fully represented, the decree was binding, and the Plaintiff was entitled to recover possession and mesne profits.
records.event: Trial Court judgment delivered
records.procedure: Court of Additional Subordinate Judge of Hazaribagh

records.text: The High Court negatived the contention regarding constructive res judicata. It considered whether Wazir Narayan Singh had power to grant the permanent lease, concluding the lease did not render the Bank's security insufficient under Section 66.
records.owner_label: High Court of Judicature at Patna
records.event: High Court judgment dismissing plaintiff's suit
records.procedure: High Court of Judicature at Patna

records.text: The High Court held the lease was valid and not affected by the Plaintiff's mortgage, decree, or execution sale, and accordingly dismissed the Plaintiff's suit. The Plaintiff obtained leave to appeal to the Privy Council.
records.owner_label: High Court of Judicature at Patna
records.event: Final High Court decision and Privy Council admission
records.procedure: High Court of Judicature at Patna

records.text: The Privy Council found the Plaintiff was subrogated to the Bank's position and Defendant 2 was sufficiently represented. The only surviving question was whether Wazir Narayan Singh had the power to grant a permanent lease to bind the Plaintiff.
records.event: Privy Council identifies sole legal question

limitations: The provided text is an excerpt from a judgment (Civil Appeal No. 73 of 1950) and does not contain the final decision or reasoning of the Privy Council regarding the specific legal question of the mortgagor's power to grant a permanent lease.
The text records the procedural history and lower court findings but does not provide the ultimate resolution of the appeal by the highest court mentioned.
